propositions: Bridge redesign consolidates fragmented Jira-specific operator commands into one provider-neutral Python-first surface with canonical verbs (setup, check-access, fsck, status, preview, sync, pause, resume) while retaining legacy reconcile and bridge-status compatibility adapters.
Canonical exit codes are 0, 1, and 2; legacy workflows depending on exit codes 3, 4, and 75 remain supported through explicit adapters.
Bridge functionality is exposed consistently across three interfaces (Python library, CLI via rebar, and MCP server) using shared core implementation with no private surface reimplementations.
Installation via brew, pip, and MCP-server all execute the same packaged Python bridge implementation without depending on editable checkouts or ambient environments.
Pause state is durable, remote-persisted, includes a reason, and remains readable by mixed-version fleets; core operations and destructive repair no longer require the gh CLI.
Tickets-branch CAS delivery and commit identity are Python-owned in src/rebar/_store/push.py and the commit-and-push entrypoint, eliminating workflow-local retry loops.
